title: Spark unified memory management and where spill comes from
purpose: Spark unified memory management. Executor heap layout; Execution memory; Storage memory; The borrowing rule; Spill and the storageFraction trap.
accessibleSummary: Spark unified memory management. Executor heap layout; Execution memory; Storage memory; The borrowing rule; Spill and the storageFraction trap.
longDescription: Spark unified memory management. Executor heap layout; Execution memory; Storage memory; The borrowing rule; Spill and the storageFraction trap.

nodes.label: Reserved — 300 MiB, fixed
nodes.summary: A fixed 300 MiB is reserved before any memory fraction is applied.
nodes.detail: A fixed 300 MiB is reserved before any memory fraction is applied.
nodes.whyItMatters: A fixed 300 MiB is reserved before any memory fraction is applied.

evidence.note: A fixed 300 MiB is reserved outside the unified region.

outputs: Usable heap for the fraction calculation
drill.example: A 16 GB heap yields roughly 15.7 GB before spark.memory.fraction applies.
failureModes: Very small executors lose a disproportionate share of heap to the fixed reservation.

nodes.label: Unified pool — fraction 0.6
nodes.summary: spark.memory.fraction sizes the shared execution and storage pool at 0.6 of the usable heap.
nodes.detail: spark.memory.fraction sizes the shared execution and storage pool at 0.6 of the usable heap.
nodes.whyItMatters: spark.memory.fraction sizes the shared execution and storage pool at 0.6 of the usable heap.

evidence.note: spark.memory.fraction defaults to 0.6 of the heap minus 300 MiB, with the remaining 40% left as headroom.

drill.example: On a 16 GB heap the shared pool is roughly 9.4 GB.
failureModes: Raising the fraction to gain working memory removes the safety headroom against large records.

nodes.label: User memory — the remaining 40%
nodes.summary: The remaining heap holds user data structures and guards against oversized records.
nodes.detail: The remaining heap holds user data structures and guards against oversized records.
nodes.whyItMatters: The remaining heap holds user data structures and guards against oversized records.

evidence.note: The 40% outside the unified region holds user data structures, internal metadata and OOM headroom.

processing: Hold user allocations outside the managed pool
outputs: Space for user structures and metadata
drill.example: Objects allocated inside a Python UDF or RDD closure live here, not in the managed pool.
failureModes: Allocating large per-row structures in user code exhausts this region and OOMs the executor.

nodes.label: Execution memory
nodes.summary: Execution memory serves shuffles, joins, sorts and aggregations and may evict storage.
nodes.detail: Execution memory serves shuffles, joins, sorts and aggregations and may evict storage.
nodes.whyItMatters: Execution memory serves shuffles, joins, sorts and aggregations and may evict storage.

evidence.note: Execution memory serves shuffles, joins, sorts and aggregations and may evict storage.
Storage cannot evict execution because of implementation complexity.

processing: Allocate working memory for sorts, joins and aggregations
outputs: In-memory computation, or spill when exhausted
drill.example: A sort-merge join builds sort buffers here and spills when the partition exceeds what it can hold.
failureModes: Oversized partitions exhaust execution memory and force disk spill.

nodes.label: Storage memory
nodes.summary: Storage memory holds cached and broadcast blocks and can never evict execution.
nodes.detail: Storage memory holds cached and broadcast blocks and can never evict execution.
nodes.whyItMatters: Storage memory holds cached and broadcast blocks and can never evict execution.

evidence.note: Storage memory holds cached blocks and broadcast variables and may use the whole pool when execution is idle.

drill.example: A dimension broadcast to every executor occupies storage memory on all of them.
failureModes: Caching a DataFrame used only once competes with execution for no benefit.

nodes.label: storageFraction is an eviction floor
nodes.summary: storageFraction sets the storage floor execution may not reclaim, not a fixed partition.
nodes.detail: storageFraction sets the storage floor execution may not reclaim, not a fixed partition.
nodes.whyItMatters: storageFraction sets the storage floor execution may not reclaim, not a fixed partition.

evidence.note: spark.memory.storageFraction defaults to 0.5 and sets the storage region immune to eviction, not a hard partition.

drill.example: At the default, roughly half the shared pool is protected from eviction once storage has claimed it.
failureModes: Treating the floor as a reservation leads to raising it and starving execution.

nodes.label: Raising storageFraction causes spill
nodes.summary: Raising the storage floor starves execution and produces the spill it was meant to avoid.
nodes.detail: Raising the storage floor starves execution and produces the spill it was meant to avoid.
nodes.whyItMatters: Raising the storage floor starves execution and produces the spill it was meant to avoid.

evidence.note: Raising the storage floor to protect a cache commonly causes the spill it was meant to prevent.
The unified model already lets execution and storage borrow, so raising storage to help caching starves execution.

processing: Overflow sort and join buffers to disk
drill.example: Stage metrics show non-zero Spill (memory) and Spill (disk) columns after a storageFraction increase.
failureModes: Every spilled byte is written once and read back, so runtime grows without any data growth.

nodes.label: Overhead is separate from the heap
nodes.summary: Executor memory overhead is requested on top of the heap and is session-start scope.
nodes.detail: Executor memory overhead is requested on top of the heap and is session-start scope.
nodes.whyItMatters: Executor memory overhead is requested on top of the heap and is session-start scope.

evidence.note: Memory outside the managed pool covers JVM internals and native allocation.

processing: Request additional overhead alongside the heap
outputs: Space for JVM internals, PySpark workers and off-heap allocation
drill.example: PySpark worker processes and native engine buffers live in overhead rather than the JVM heap.
failureModes: Undersized overhead OOMs an executor in a way that looks like a data problem but is not.

edges.label: Floor bounds what execution may evict
Exhausted execution memory spills to disk
Overhead is requested outside the heap
